beats.say: This star has no straight lines in it. It's drawn only by spinning circles. Here's how many it takes.

head: 1 CIRCLE:
A CIRCLE.
beats.say: One spinning circle on its own draws, well, a circle. Nothing else.

head: 2 CIRCLES:
IT BENDS.
beats.say: Put a second circle on the tip of the first, spinning faster. Now the path bends.

head: 3 CIRCLES:
5 POINTS.
beats.say: Three circles. Five points start to show.

head: 10 CIRCLES:
SHARP.
beats.say: Ten circles, and the points get sharp. Each new circle is smaller than the one before.

head: 50 CIRCLES:
A STAR.
beats.say: Fifty circles. A clean star. Every single corner made from turning wheels.

head: THIS IS A
FOURIER SERIES.
beats.say: This is a Fourier series, named for Joseph Fourier. Shapes and signals built from sines and cosines, and each spinning circle is one of them.
Follow Ship With Pip for more.

title: This star has no straight lines. Just spinning circles
caption: Every circle spins at its own speed on the tip of the one before it. 1 circle draws a circle. 2 bend it. 3 show 5 points. 10 make them sharp, and 50 draw a clean star. This is a Fourier series: a sum of sines and cosines, named for Joseph Fourier, and each spinning circle is one term. The circles here come from a discrete Fourier transform of the star's outline, biggest first.
notes: Star: 5 points, inner radius 0.42, sampled at 1024 points, DFT, circles sorted by size (largest first, constant term excluded). Beats show n = 1, 2, 3, 10, 50 circles. Britannica: a Fourier series is an infinite sum of sines and cosines, named for Joseph Fourier. A spinning circle traces e^(ikt) = cos(kt) + i sin(kt).
